newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU invites members to recall ambassadors from Iran.
newsitem.headline: EU invites members to recall ambassadors from Iran.

text.p: The European Union invited member countries on Thursday to recall their ambassadors from Iran following a German court ruling accusinh Iranian leaders of ordering the killing of exiled Kurds.

"The presidency invited member states to recall their ambassadors for coordinated consultations on the future relationship of the European Union with Iran," said Dutch Foreign Ministry spokesman Peter Mollema, whose country holds the EU presidency until the end of June.
Germany on Thursday ordered four Iranian diplomats out of the country after a Berlin court decision implicating Teheran in ordering the assassination of four Kurdish Iranian leaders in 1992.

Presiding judge Frithjof Kubsch said the killing was on the orders of a special operations committee whose members included Iran's president, its religious leader, Intelligence Minister and head of foreign policy.

He stopped short of explicitly naming Iranian President Ali Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani and religious leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who had been accused by prosecutors of ultimate resposibility for the attack in Berlin's Mykonos restaurant.

"In the findings of the superior court of Justice in Berlin in the so-called Mykonos case, the involvement of Iranian authorities was established. This is condemned and we regard such behaviour as totally unacceptable in the conduct of international affairs," Mollema said.
He stressed that the EU had invited member states to recall their ambassadors for consultations and had not ordered them out of Teheran. Germany has already recalled its ambassador.

"The EU has always wanted a constructive relationship with Iran, and its 'critical dialogue' agreed at the European Council in 1992 was designed to further that objective. However no progress can be possible while Iran flouts international norms and indulges in acts of terrorism," Mollema said, reading from an official EU statement.

An EU declaration in 1992 said a critical dialogue should be maintained with Iran, but it should reflect concern about Iranian behaviour and calls for improvement in a number of areas including human rights.
Mollema said a European Council meeting on April 29 would review the EU's relations with Iran and decide what further action was appropriate.
The EU also warned Iran that it would not tolerate any reprisals against European citizens in the country.

"The EU expects the Iranian government to take measures against possible threats...against any member states and to take the necessary steps to safeguard the security of all European citizens and institutions in Iran," the statement said.
